decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation: “Save a bookmark — enter a URL ... stored”; round 1 client did not contest URL-based saving.
decisions.note: The baseline save decision conforms at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation offered only “Auto-fetch page titles”; round 1 client required collecting “description, site icon, and preview image.”
decisions.note: The initial metadata scope omitted three required fields; corrected at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation did not specify editing fetched metadata; round 1 client said “I should be able to edit the title and description.”
decisions.note: The client added required editing of collected metadata at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation included “remove links, with a confirmation before deletion”; the client did not contest deletion.
decisions.note: Deletion was conforming in the initial specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation: duplicate detection “warns”; round 1 client: re-saving “should take me to the existing bookmark so I can edit it, rather than merely warning me.”
decisions.note: The client replaced warning-only duplicate handling with edit-existing behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation described only “browse” and did not identify title, description, tags, and favicon per row; round 1 response did not raise list-row contents.
decisions.note: The first specification presented an underspecified list without a response addressing the missing readability fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation did not state that list selection opens the original URL; round 1 client required “selecting it from the list should open the original page.”
decisions.note: Missing navigation behavior was added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation included “tag bookmarks, and filter by tag”; round 1 client accepted tags as the organization mechanism.
decisions.note: Assignment and filtering by a specific tag conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation included tagging but no autocomplete; round 1 client said “Existing tags should be suggested while I type.”
decisions.note: Tag autocomplete was missing from the initial specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation limited keyword search to “title/URL/tags”; round 1 client required descriptions and notes to be searched too.
decisions.note: The initial full-text field set omitted description and note.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation did not define case handling; round 1 client required search to be “case-insensitive.”
decisions.note: Case-insensitive search was supplied as a missing requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation mentioned keyword search but no tag syntax; round 1 client requested “`#tag` searches.”
Round 1 presentation had no Boolean grammar; round 1 client requested “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.”
decisions.note: Boolean operators and grouping were missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation had no phrase syntax; round 1 client requested “quoted phrases.”
Round 1 presentation omitted read-later behavior; round 1 client requested “a read-later state with a separate unread view” and marking items read.
decisions.note: The complete unread workflow was added at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation omitted bulk operations; round 1 client required selecting several bookmarks or all current results for shared actions.
decisions.note: Multi-select and whole-filter bulk actions were missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation gave no sorting control; round 1 client said “The list needs sorting options.”
Round 1 presentation omitted notes; round 1 client required “a personal note.”
decisions.note: Bookmark notes were absent from the initial specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation omitted snapshots; round 1 client requested a preserved local page copy, “with PDFs saved as PDFs.”
Round 1 presentation omitted external archival; round 1 client requested “an option to save a copy through the Internet Archive.”
decisions.note: Internet Archive snapshot support was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation only described deletion; round 1 client required reversible archiving, default/search exclusion, and a separate archived view.
decisions.note: The archive lifecycle and its distinction from deletion were missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation omitted bundles; round 1 client requested “saved reusable filters” containing search terms and included/excluded tags.
Round 1 presentation listed import/export only as a possible omission; round 1 client explicitly required browser-bookmark HTML import and export preserving titles, tags, and dates.
decisions.note: Both interchange directions were added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation omitted profile display settings; round 1 client required default sorting, item count, and text-size preferences.
Round 2 presentation: “Capture title, description, favicon, preview image”; round 2 client did not contest those collected fields.
decisions.note: The revised metadata field set conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation merely said “edit title & description”; round 2 client clarified they must be editable “both while saving and afterward.”
decisions.note: The timing of metadata editing remained incomplete and was corrected.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation offered a persistent personal note but did not specify Markdown rendering; round 2 client required “simple Markdown formatting” and formatted display.
Round 2 presentation: “selecting opens original in new tab”; round 2 client did not object.
Round 2 presentation: re-saving a known URL “opens the existing bookmark to edit” and creates no duplicate.
Round 2 presentation specified case-insensitive search over title/URL/description/note, `#tag`, and quoted phrases; the response did not reject these parts.

Round 2 presentation listed Boolean operators and parentheses but omitted conjunction and quoting rules; round 2 client required text plus `#tag` to both match unless `OR`, and quoted operators to be literal text.
decisions.note: The Boolean grammar was incomplete and the client supplied the required semantics.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation included suggesting existing tags while typing.
Round 2 presentation said suggestions avoid duplicate variants but did not guarantee uniqueness for typed tags; round 2 client required tag names to remain unique even when typed.
Round 2 presentation included unread state, a separate unread view, and marking read.
decisions.note: The read-later workflow conformed at this stage, aside from the later-discovered creation default.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation included multi-select and “all in current results” actions for tags/read/archive/delete.
Round 2 presentation offered newest, oldest, title, and last-updated sorting.
Round 2 presentation made archiving reversible, excluded archived items from normal list/search, and provided a dedicated view.
Round 2 presentation described named saved filters from terms plus included/excluded tags.
Round 2 presentation specified standard bookmark HTML with titles, tags, and dates preserved.
Round 2 presentation promised an offline-readable local copy and PDFs as PDFs but did not specify single-file HTML; round 2 client required “a self-contained single file.”
decisions.note: The HTML snapshot representation remained incomplete.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation included the Internet Archive option; the client explicitly accepted graceful failure when the service is unreachable.
decisions.note: Internet Archive support conformed; graceful failure is not a reference divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation included persisted default sort, items per view, and text size.
Round 2 presentation still did not specify list-row fields; round 2 client required every normal-list item to visibly include title, description, tags, and site icon.
decisions.note: The list readability requirement was caught in the second specification review.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation: “Notes support simple Markdown, shown formatted”; round 3 client approved the revised specification.
Round 3 presentation: title and description editable “while saving and after”; round 3 client approved.
Round 3 presentation: list items show “title, description, tags, site icon”; round 3 client approved.
Round 3 presentation specified implicit conjunction for text plus `#tag` and quoted operators as literals; round 3 client approved.
Round 3 presentation made tag names unique even when typed; round 3 client approved.
Round 3 presentation defined the local copy as a self-contained single file opening offline; round 3 client approved.
Round 4 plan used fetch/Cheerio with a browser fallback for title, description, social preview data, and favicon.
decisions.note: The planned metadata implementation was functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 plan chose a parser/AST specifically for implicit AND, quoted-operator literals, and `#tag` semantics.
Round 4 plan specified one self-contained HTML file, PDFs stored as-is, and Internet Archive Save Page Now.
Round 4 plan used Netscape bookmark HTML with merge-by-URL.
Round 4 plan stored Markdown and rendered it with sanitization.
Round 4 plan’s data-model decision made new bookmarks unread; round 4 client said they must start as ordinary read items. Round 5 maker confirmed the default was “changed to 1 = read.”
decisions.note: The wrong initial read state was corrected at the plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 plan claimed saved filters and select-all endpoints but did not carry included/excluded tags through the result request; round 4 client required all conditions, and round 5 maker added `include_tags`/`exclude_tags`.
decisions.note: Saved-filter application and whole-result bulk scope were incomplete.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 plan did not define snapshot-file lifecycle on delete versus archive; round 4 client required permanent delete to remove the local copy while archive retains it.
decisions.note: The permanent-removal consequence was added at the plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presentation changed `is_read` to default to read and required deliberate marking for later; round 5 client approved.
Round 5 presentation threaded query, view, included tags, and excluded tags through listing and select-all; round 5 client approved.
Round 5 presentation made permanent delete remove the on-disk copy and archive retain it; round 5 client approved.
Round 6 task presentation covered metadata capture, bookmark/tag models, save/list endpoints, and rows with title/description/tags/icon.
Round 6 tasks combined metadata fetching with bookmark creation; round 6 client required a preview before final save so fetched title/description could be edited.
decisions.note: The task design did not support pre-save metadata editing.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 tasks included sanitized Markdown notes and opening the original URL.
Round 6 tasks included edit-on-duplicate.
Round 6 tasks included the search parser/evaluator and tests for the approved grammar.
decisions.note: The task breakdown covered the reference search requirements. The client’s additional request that ordinary words match tag names is beyond REF-BM-12’s enumerated full-text fields and is not treated as a divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 tasks included tag suggestions.
Round 6 tasks included read-later behavior and pinned `is_read` default 1.
Round 6 tasks included archiving and the approved lifecycle behavior.
Round 6 tasks included bulk actions and select-all with complete filter conditions.
decisions.note: General bulk selection and scope conformed, separate from file cleanup on bulk delete.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 cleanup task covered only single-item deletion; round 6 client required bulk deletion to remove every selected bookmark’s local page-copy file.
decisions.note: Bulk permanent deletion omitted associated snapshot cleanup.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 tasks included sorting.
Round 6 tasks included saved filters with the corrected condition threading.
Round 6 tasks included import/export and a round-trip test.
Round 6 tasks included local page copies and Internet Archive support.
decisions.note: Snapshot task coverage conformed apart from the separately classified bulk-delete cleanup.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 tasks included preferences.
Round 7 presentation added a metadata-only endpoint, editable preview, and final creation using user-edited values; round 7 client approved.
decisions.note: The revised pre-save editing flow conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 presentation required a shared cleanup helper for both single and bulk delete, never archive; round 7 client approved.
Round 8 presentation reported implemented metadata, search, Markdown, snapshot, Internet Archive, and import/export services with passing unit/smoke checks.
decisions.note: The presented service behaviors matched the reference; limited exhaustive live-network exercise did not itself establish a functional divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 presentation said the running app was ready and exposed its controls; round 8 client found “the whole page is dimmed,” an empty modal blocked the page, and “the controls cannot be used,” and requested corrected hidden-state behavior.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the always-visible overlay prevented use of the reference UI behaviors.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 presentation claimed a functional bulk bar; round 8 client observed “An empty bulk-action bar is also visible even though nothing is selected” and required it to remain absent until triggered.
decisions.note: The bulk-action presentation contradicted its selection-triggered interaction at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 presentation claimed visible read-later and archive views; round 8 client did not identify their invisible labels. Round 9 maker independently reported a second defect: inactive Unread/Archive labels were “white-on-transparent (invisible).”
decisions.note: Discoverability of the separate views diverged in the first implementation presentation without a client response addressing that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 presentation added `[hidden] { display: none !important; }` and reported successful click-through of dialogs, tabs, search, sort, and edit; round 9 client said the app was usable and accepted it.
Round 9 presentation verified the bulk bar appears only after selection and disappears on deselection; round 9 client accepted the application.
Round 9 presentation gave view tabs explicit readable text and verified All/Unread/Archive were clickable; round 9 client confirmed navigation and controls were visible.
